critique.evidence: The headline, supporting sentence, and “WHAT’S HAPPENING” copy clearly establish the claim and explicitly instruct users to filter the atlas and select a vector. Agentic/Classic/All and kill-chain controls are labeled, while the selected vector’s title, severity, stage, and observable signals create a clear desktop reading path. However, tablet and especially mobile crop the stage columns and make the kill-chain diagram extremely small; much of the 48-vector atlas is off-screen with no visible cue that horizontal navigation is required. The vector cards also lack a strong affordance showing that they are selectable.
critique.fix: On tablet and mobile, replace the wide stage board with a responsive stacked list or clearly signposted horizontal scroller with stage navigation. Increase the kill-chain diagram’s legibility, add an explicit selected/hover/tap affordance to vector cards, and keep the selected vector detail adjacent to its source card.
